name: Build a Modern Calculator with React & Tailwind CSS
description: A hands-on, project-based tutorial to build a fully functional, stylish calculator web app. Master React fundamentals (state, hooks, components) and modern CSS with Tailwind while implementing core features like keyboard support and safe math evaluation.
projectOverview: You will build a calculator that supports basic arithmetic operations (+, -, *, /), features a clear and delete functionality, handles user input from both mouse and keyboard, and displays a clean, responsive interface. The final app will be deployed live on the web.
whatYouLearn: Set up a modern React development environment with Vite
Structure a React application with reusable components
Manage application state effectively using the useState hook
Handle user events (clicks, keyboard presses) in React
Style a complete application using Tailwind CSS utility classes
Use the useEffect hook for side effects (keyboard events)
Build and deploy a production-ready app to a platform like Vercel
prerequisites: Basic understanding of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (ES6+ syntax)
Familiarity with Node.js and npm is recommended
A code editor (like VS Code) and a terminal

exercises.title: Project Setup & Tooling
exercises.description: Initialize your React project using Vite for a fast development experience and integrate Tailwind CSS for styling.
exercises.theory: We use Vite as our build tool because it offers lightning-fast server start and hot module replacement. Tailwind CSS is a utility-first framework that allows us to style our application directly in our JSX, leading to rapid UI development.
exercises.objective: Create a new React project and configure Tailwind CSS.
exercises.initialCode:
# Let's create the project scaffold. Run this in your terminal:
npm create vite@latest react-calculator -- --template react
cd react-calculator
npm install
requirements: Initialize a Vite React project
Install and configure Tailwind CSS
Start the development server
hints: Vite's `create` command is the modern equivalent of Create React App.
The `content` array in `tailwind.config.js` tells Tailwind which files to scan for class names.

exercises.title: Building the Component Scaffold
exercises.description: Create the foundational JSX structure for the calculator, breaking it down into logical components.
exercises.theory: React applications are built using components—reusable, self-contained pieces of UI. We'll structure our calculator with a main `App` component that houses a `Display` component and a `Button` component.
exercises.objective: Create the Display and Button components and assemble them in App.jsx.
requirements: Create Display and Button components
Build the main calculator layout in App.jsx
Apply initial Tailwind CSS styles for a clean look
hints: Use CSS Grid (`grid grid-cols-4`) for the button layout. It's perfect for this use case.
The `font-mono` class on the display gives it a classic calculator font.

exercises.title: Adding Interactivity with State
exercises.description: Make the calculator buttons functional by managing the display value and user input with React state.
exercises.theory: The `useState` Hook lets you add state to functional components. The calculator's display value, the current input string, and the result are all pieces of state that change over time based on user interaction.
exercises.objective: Use useState to manage the calculator's display and handle button click events.
requirements: Implement useState to manage input and result
Create a handleButtonClick function to process user input
Pass click handlers and props down to child components
Differentiate button styles based on their function (number, operator, etc.)
hints: Use functional updates (`setInput(prev => prev + value)`) for state that depends on the previous state.
The `buttonLayout` array makes the JSX cleaner and easier to modify.

exercises.title: Implementing Robust Calculation Logic
exercises.description: Replace the basic `eval` logic with a safer, more controlled calculation function to handle arithmetic operations correctly.
exercises.theory: While `eval()` and `Function()` can work, they are security risks and can be unpredictable. For a production calculator, it's better to implement a parser or use a library. We'll build a simple, safe evaluator for our four basic operations.
exercises.objective: Create a safe calculation function and integrate it into the app.
exercises.initialCode:
// Let's create a utility function for calculations
// Create a new file: src/utils/calculate.js
requirements: Create a safe calculate function in a separate utility file
Implement input validation and error handling
Add percentage functionality
Prevent invalid input patterns (like multiple decimal points)
hints: The regex `/^[\d+\-*/.()]+$/` ensures only valid calculator characters are used.
For a real-world app, consider using a library like `mathjs` for advanced and safe mathematical operations.

exercises.title: Enhancing UX with Keyboard Support & Animation
exercises.description: Add keyboard event listeners so users can type calculations and include subtle animations for a polished feel.
exercises.theory: The `useEffect` hook lets you perform side effects in function components. We'll use it to add and remove a global keyboard event listener. We'll also use Tailwind's transition classes for visual feedback.
exercises.objective: Implement keyboard input support and refine button animations.
exercises.initialCode:
// We'll use the useEffect hook to add keyboard support
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
requirements: Use useEffect to add keyboard event listeners
Map common keyboard keys (Enter, Escape, Backspace) to calculator functions
Enhance button animations with hover and active states
Add focus styles for accessibility
hints: The dependency array in `useEffect` ensures our event listener has the latest state.
The `active:scale-95` and `hover:scale-105` classes provide satisfying tactile feedback.

exercises.title: Deployment & Production Build
exercises.description: Build your application for production and deploy it to a hosting platform like Vercel or Netlify.
exercises.theory: Vite pre-bundles your code and optimizes it for production, creating static files that can be served by any web server. Platforms like Vercel and Netlify offer seamless deployment for frontend applications, often directly from your Git repository.
exercises.objective: Create a production build and deploy it online.
exercises.initialCode:
# First, let's create a production build
npm run build
exercises.solutionCode:
# 1. Create a production build
npm run build

# This creates a `dist` folder with optimized production files.

# 2. Deploy using Vercel (easiest method):
# Option A: Using the Vercel CLI
npm install -g vercel
vercel --prod

# Option B: Using Git (Recommended)
# - Push your code to a GitHub repository.
# - Go to vercel.com and sign up with your GitHub account.
# - Click "New Project" and import your calculator repository.
# - Vercel will automatically detect it's a Vite app and configure the settings.
# - Click "Deploy". Your app will be live in seconds!

# 3. Alternatively, deploy to Netlify:
# - Push your code to GitHub.
# - Go to netlify.com, sign up, and click "Add new site" -> "Import an existing project".
# - Connect your GitHub repo.
# - Set the build command to `npm run build` and publish directory to `dist`.
# - Click "Deploy site`.
requirements: Run a production build
Deploy the application to a live URL
Verify the deployed application works correctly
hints: The `dist` folder is all you need to host your app. Don't upload your `src` or `node_modules`.
If your app doesn't load on Vercel/Netlify, check if you need a `vite.config.js` file with the correct base setting: `export default { base: './' }`

nextSteps: Add a calculation history feature that shows previous operations.
Implement scientific calculator functions (sin, cos, tan, log, etc.).
Add theme switcher (light mode/dark mode) using React Context.
Convert the app to use TypeScript for better type safety.
Add unit and integration tests with Jest and React Testing Library.
